summary.headline: Jana SFB met all Q4 FY26 guidance: PAT INR140 crore, net credit cost 0.47%, SMA 3.66%; FY27 guided to PAT growth of 80%+.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered on every guidance point set in Q3: PAT of INR140 crore (guided INR140-160 crore), net credit cost of 0.47% (INR156 crore) against 0.79% in Q3, and SMA of 3.66% versus a guided ceiling of below 4%. Gross slippages of about INR334 crore were the lowest in roughly eight quarters, and management said the MFI stress is behind it. Advances grew 23% YoY to INR36,289 crore and deposits grew 23% to INR35,784 crore, with cost of funds down to 7.46%. FY27 guidance calls for gross loan growth of 19-21%, deposit growth of 23-25% and PAT growth of 80%+.

segments.name: Affordable housing
segments.commentary: Largest product at INR8,174 crore with average ticket of INR12.7 lakh. Relocations and split branches were the main FY26 branch drivers.

segments.name: Micro LAP
segments.commentary: INR6,300 crore book with average ticket of INR6.7 lakh, growing only 9.4% YoY and the weakest secured segment; management expects 12-15% growth in FY27.

segments.name: MSME / commercial banking
segments.commentary: INR5,281 crore MSME book, with commercial banking growing about 23.3%; management is watching for Middle East war spillover.

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: INR2,358 crore book, up 140% YoY, average ticket about INR2 lakh; yields said to be competitive with market but below gold NBFCs.

segments.name: Vehicle loans (2-wheeler and used car)
segments.commentary: Vehicle loans grew 79.6% YoY. Used car business launched October 2025, running at about INR25 crore disbursals per month in 15 cities, targeted to reach 35 cities by September 2026.

segments.name: Microfinance (MFI)
segments.commentary: MFI book was about INR10,000 crore in March 2024 and INR8,900 crore in March 2025, and has risen about 10% since but is still below March 2024. Unsecured slippages were about INR150 crore in Q4, down 35% QoQ and about 50% YoY; the SMA book fell about 24%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 gross loan portfolio growth of 19-21%, deposit growth of 23-25%, and PAT growth of 80%+ over FY26; guidance excludes any benefit from a possible universal bank licence.
Secured book to grow 25-30% and unsecured 10-12% in FY27; total secured advances growth expected closer to 30% in FY27.
Cost of deposits: Q1 FY27 expected to be the low point after one more quarter of decline, then flat; NIM to improve through unsecured growth.
Credit cost for FY27 not guided explicitly; management indicated a range similar to or slightly better than Q4's 0.47%.
CASA growth expected at 27-30% in FY27; branches to rise from 822 to about 860 (30 splits, 8 new, 40 relocations), with cost growth to taper sharply versus FY26.

CGMFU guarantee claim expected to be filed July-August 2026, with first payout around October 2026 (rough estimate INR65 crore in Q3 FY27). Guaranteed share of unsecured book at 77.1%, expected to reach 90-95%.
Cost-to-income targeted below 60% over time; management says March 2024 level of 57% is the reference point. Launch of UPI-linked credit line and AD1 forex licence expected in FY27.
capex_capacity: 80 branches added in FY26 (12 new, 26 splits, 42 relocations); network reached 822 branches.
FY27 plan: 78 branch actions (30 splits, 8 new, 40 relocations), taking the network to about 860 branches.
RM and sales investments made in FY26 are said to be sufficient for 20-25% growth without significant new investment.
Used car business: 15 cities, targeting 35 cities by September 2026.

Management said FY27 cost growth will taper sharply versus FY26, which included INR77 crore of upfront disbursement costs, INR55 crore of guarantee programme costs, and INR55 crore of investment, collections and used-car costs.
demand_pricing: Management reports no customer pricing decline across products (MFI, housing, LAP, MSME).
Unsecured disbursements hit a record in Q4; management says fewer competitors are active post-stress, leaving unmet demand and a window of advantage.
April 2026: collections at 99%+ for both BC and in-house MFI books, with an April SMA cycle that management says is far better than April 2025.
Deposit market: management says 84% of new industry deposits are term deposits and only 16% CASA; no visible liquidity tightness in April.
Term-deposit borrowings from NABARD, SIDBI and NHB at about 6.9-7% blended on 10-year tenure, against deposit cost of about 7.46%. Refinance funding is about 12-15% of the book.

qa_highlights.question: Will NIM expand in the coming quarters, especially from unsecured?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NIM improved in Q4 from lower slippages and reduced interest in suspense plus 10% QoQ unsecured growth. Q1 FY27 should see cost of deposits fall and NIM improve; Q2 onwards should show flat deposit costs with a slight NIM gain.

qa_highlights.question: Will the MFI and unsecured slippage decline continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Unsecured slippages were about INR150 crore in Q4, down 35% QoQ and about 50% YoY, and the SMA book fell about 24%. Management expects further lower slippages in FY27 but not a steep decline, since collections are at 99%.

qa_highlights.question: Any stress in MSME, micro LAP or housing?
qa_highlights.answer: Micro LAP was tightened in some geographies last year and management sees no signs of stress. MSME is being watched for Middle East war spillover, and nothing is visible yet.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for credit cost next year?
qa_highlights.answer: No explicit guidance. Management pointed to the Q4 net credit cost of 0.47% as a signal, expecting the same range or slightly better.

qa_highlights.question: Gold loan yields and FY27 MFI growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold yields are competitive for about INR2 lakh tickets but below gold NBFCs. Yields should rise as MFI customers take smaller-ticket gold loans. Secured MFI book to grow 25-30% and unsecured MFI 10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: Universal bank reapplication and CASA growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Reapplication work restarts now that audited results are out; gross NPA of 3% and net NPA of 1% are gating criteria. FY27 guidance excludes any benefit from universal bank status. CASA is guided to grow 27-30%.

qa_highlights.question: Cost of deposits, borrowing cost and cost-to-income?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 FY27 is expected to be the lowest cost-of-deposit point, then flat. Recent borrowings were 10-year NABARD/SIDBI/NHB funds at about 6.9-7%, to improve ALM. Cost-to-income is targeted below 60%, against 57% in March 2024.

risks_watch: Q4 CASA fell about 8% QoQ after government CASA withdrawals; management is trying to recover it, and CASA growth of 27-30% is the target.
Middle East war impact on MSME and retail borrowers (for example, petrol pump fuel supply cut); management says it is unclear and being monitored.
Universal bank reapplication: outcome and timing uncertain, and the company says it is not in the numbers.
CGMFU guarantee recoveries (about INR65 crore expected in Q3 FY27) and the timing of claims.
Cost growth discipline versus the 80%+ PAT growth guidance; the cost-to-income target is below 60%.
Micro LAP recovery to 12-15% growth after 9.4% growth in FY26, and a deposit cost decline that management expects to stop after Q1 FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident and specific on Q4 delivery, guidance achievement and April collections, with management calling the MFI stress over. Cautious on the external environment (Middle East war, MSME) and on CASA, where Q4 was a setback that management is still working to recover.
